clue.text: Vulgar jester not on for comic part in opera

indicators.note: not means the following word is to be left out of the jester

parts.note: a vulgar jester is a buffoon, a coarse clown
taken as written

explanation.surface: A coarse clown is turned away from playing the funny role in an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not on' tells you to remove ON from BUFFOON.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for a comic singer, used for the comic bass role in opera buffa.

clue.text: Flat holder in short suit

parts.note: brief means short
a case is a lawsuit

explanation.surface: Someone carries a flat bag while wearing a short suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A slim bag for carrying papers, which lie flat inside.

clue.text: Game of Rugby at Eton?

parts.note: the handball court game played in versions named after the schools of Rugby and Eton

explanation.surface: Asks whether Eton plays Rugby's football code.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby and Eton are English public schools, each giving its name to a version of this handball game.
explanation.definitionFit: A handball game played in a walled court, with Rugby and Eton varieties.

clue.text: Ostracised, perhaps, over a single broadcast

parts.note: on means over, as in a lid on a jar
one means a single
broadcast seed is sown, scattered

explanation.surface: Someone shunned, perhaps after a single programme went out.
explanation.definitionFit: An ostracised person is left alone, without company.

clue.text: A quick test for measles?

parts.note: a random brief inspection, read literally as checking someone for the red marks of measles

explanation.surface: A doctor wonders about a rapid way to diagnose measles.
explanation.definitionFit: A random quick inspection; measles shows as red marks on the skin, so checking for them is literally looking at marks.

clue.text: One of the algae found in the main dock, for example

parts.note: the main is the sea
dock is a weed, so it is an example of one

explanation.surface: Algae turn up in a harbour dock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dock' looks like a harbour but is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Kelp and wrack are marine algae.

clue.text: Decorated silk creation requires a needle

parts.note: the OBE is a British decoration, Order of the British Empire

indicators.note: creation means the letters of silk are made into something new

explanation.surface: Making an embroidered silk garment calls for a needle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creation' signals an anagram of SILK, giving LISK.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall stone pillars such as Cleopatra's Needle in London.

clue.text: It divides a long poem into pious platitudes on love

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the love letter sits beneath the platitudes

parts.note: cant is hypocritical pious talk
love is nil, O, in tennis

explanation.surface: A long poem breaks down into sanctimonious remarks about love.
explanation.definitionFit: A major section of a long poem, as in Dante.

clue.text: Difficult clue — guess name of mathematician

indicators.note: difficult means the letters of clue are troublesome and rearranged

parts.note: an idea is a guess

explanation.surface: A solver finds the clue hard and guesses a mathematician's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Difficult' signals an anagram of CLUE, giving EUCL.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to Euclid, the Greek geometer.

clue.text: King has mistress — does that ring a bell?

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
Nell Gwyn was mistress to King Charles II

explanation.surface: Asks if the story of a king's mistress sounds familiar.
explanation.definitionFit: The tolling of a bell for a death.

clue.text: Popular fiddle — the note is pure

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable
a viola is a fiddle in the loose sense of a bowed string instrument
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A fashionable violinist plays a note that rings perfectly clean.
explanation.definitionFit: Untouched and unbroken, hence free from violation or stain.

clue.text: Recess for an hour in pleasant surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings means the pleasant word is placed around the hour

parts.note: nice means pleasant
h is the standard abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: A break of an hour in a nice setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A small recess or alcove in a wall, typically for a statue.

clue.text: Enemy captures ship in the Canal

indicators.note: captures means the enemy takes in the ship, holding it inside

parts.note: a foe is an enemy
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: An enemy seizes a vessel in the canal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captures' is the container signal: the enemy holds the ship inside it. 'Canal' is fair because a fosse is a dug channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A ditch or artificial waterway, the old word for a dug channel.

clue.text: Leader produces adroit lie

indicators.note: produces means the letters of the following words are worked up into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper's lead article is a clever falsehood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produces' signals an anagram of ADROIT LIE.
explanation.definitionFit: In British newspapers a leader is the leading article stating the paper's opinion.

clue.text: Welsh sailor gets a place out east

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman

indicators.note: out means the compass point is removed from the place

parts.note: second is a place, as in finishing second in a race

explanation.surface: A sailor from Wales finds somewhere to live out in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes E from SECOND to leave SCOND. 'Welsh' looks like a nationality but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To welsh is to slip away without paying a debt, i.e. to run off secretly.

clue.text: Discard a club? No — it may be used again

parts.note: to scrap is to discard
an iron is a golf club

explanation.surface: A golfer considers throwing away a club, then decides it can be used again.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste metal collected for recycling.

clue.text: Line on Jack's wrongdoing

indicators.note: on means the line comes placed after the card name

parts.note: the knave is the jack in a pack of cards
RY is an abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A line about the misdeeds of someone called Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means placed after, so the railway abbreviation comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishonest roguery, the conduct of a rogue.

clue.text: Taking long drop at the end of a rope

definitions.text: Taking long drop at the end of a rope

parts.words: Taking long drop at the end of a rope
parts.note: sounds like hanging, but describes a climber descending a cliff on a rope

explanation.surface: Sounds like an execution by hanging.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray apostrophe in the clue as held is an OCR mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Descending a rock face on a doubled rope, a climbing technique.

clue.text: Chinese waters the drink — it's egg-coloured on top

indicators.note: on top in a down clue means the colour sits above the drink

parts.note: the colour of egg yolk is yellow
the drink is slang for the sea

explanation.surface: Someone eyes the water off China and notes its yolk-like hue.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea between China and Korea.

clue.text: Ireland, back in the century, was peace-loving

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland

indicators.note: back means the short phrase for in the century is read from the end

parts.note: taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century

explanation.surface: In the past century Ireland was a peaceful nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns 'in the century' (IN C) to give NIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Conciliatory, aiming at peace; from the Greek word for peace.

clue.text: A lot left this section of the church

parts.note: a lot, as drawn by lots, is chance

explanation.surface: Many people have left this part of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of a church near the altar for clergy and choir.

clue.text: Club magazine

definitions.meaning: a store of weapons and ammunition

explanation.surface: A football club's fanzine.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a north London football team and a store for arms and munitions.

clue.text: Tact in speech

definitions.meaning: skill and adroitness in handling people
a formal talk to an audience

explanation.surface: Tactfulness when giving a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Means both deftness in dealing with others and a formal oration.

clue.text: It shortens and 'amstrings it

parts.note: hamstrings, said with a dropped h, means hampers, cripples, also with its h dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sign that abbreviates the word and, said in a Cockney voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamstrings' with the h dropped gives 'AMPERS (hampers, dropped h). The symbol & shortens the written word 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: The symbol & is a short way of writing the conjunction joining two words.

clue.text: A godmother's first warning

parts.note: a lar is a Roman household god (plural Lares)

indicators.note: first means take only the opening letter of mother

explanation.surface: A fairy godmother's earliest caution.
explanation.definitionFit: A signal alerting people to danger.

clue.text: Governance by King Emperor

parts.note: rule is governance
R is for Rex, Latin king

explanation.surface: Government by a king-emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray apostrophe in the clue as held is an OCR mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign who governs.

clue.text: One degree turn by butterfly, for example

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MA is a Master of Arts degree
a go is a turn, as in a game

explanation.surface: A small rotation made by a butterfly.
explanation.definitionFit: The final adult stage of an insect, a butterfly being one instance.

clue.text: A bar opposite middle of ship

parts.note: a beam is a bar of timber or metal

explanation.surface: A bar facing the middle of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical: at right angles to the vessel's length, level with its middle.

clue.text: Girl in trouble about publicity

indicators.note: about means the trouble word goes round the publicity

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
PR is public relations, publicity

explanation.surface: A young woman in a scandal over press coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal: the trouble word goes round the publicity abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, from the spring month.

clue.text: Bentley's Brief Lives

parts.note: the comic four-line biographical verses invented by Edmund Clerihew Bentley, echoing Aubrey's book title Brief Lives

explanation.surface: The title of a book of short biographies by someone named Bentley.
explanation.walkthrough: John Aubrey's 'Brief Lives' is a famous 17th-century set of short biographies; E. C. Bentley wrote short comic verses about famous people, named after his middle name.
explanation.definitionFit: Humorous four-line verses about a famous person, a form created by E. C. Bentley.

clue.text: Source of the Mekong, with little streams, where baboons are found

indicators.note: the source of a river is where it starts, so take the first letter of Mekong

parts.note: and means with, together
rills are small brooks

explanation.surface: Baboons live near the headwaters of the Mekong, among its small streams.
explanation.definitionFit: Large West African baboons with bright red and blue faces.

clue.text: Stop in the country when I go

indicators.note: go means the letter I departs from the country's name

parts.note: Gambia is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: A traveller rests in a country when they leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when I go' takes I out of GAMBIA.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ stop with a string tone, named after the viola da gamba.
